summary: Sidecar connection thundering causing reserved-pool slot latch & transient throughput collapse
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 12:07 and 12:35 UTC, a customer (DataMuse - dedicated pool) observed a sharp drop in sustained throughput and elevated p99 latency on batched generation routes. Impact: multiple short-lived requests from many clients produced a sidecar connection storm which led to transient GPU slot reservations ('slot latch') and prefetch starvation for batched streams; customer reported 40-60% reduction in tokens/sec for 20 minutes. Environment: production reserved pool in us-east; Dedicated capacity cluster: rp-us-east-07; Serving runtime v2.8.1, sidecar-proxy v1.5.3, scheduler v0.9.4.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic pattern: thousands of very short streams (median duration ~150ms) originating from a fanout of ~200 client endpoints hitting the same model route.
2) Sidecar proxies opened and closed connections rapidly; many connections reset mid-handshake.
3) Scheduler observed many transient slot allocations marked in-use while sidecar tracked heartbeat state; prefetch jobs queued but did not complete due to slot latch timing out.
4) Autoscaler did not trigger immediate scale-up (thresholds tuned to sustained queue depth) -> reserved pool maintained same slot count and p99 drift persisted.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- serving-runtime: "[12:12:17Z] slot-reserve: id=slot-78f, state=HELD_BY_SIDECAR, lease=30s"
- sidecar-proxy: "[12:12:18Z] conn: accept fd=210 remote=10.3.99.42:54321 state=ESTABLISHED -> RESET"
- scheduler: "[12:12:19Z] prefetch: id=pref-412 queued (dep: slot-78f) waiting for attach"
- k8s events: repeated CrashLoopBackOff on sidecar-reporter (metric handshake spikes)

Observed metrics: sudden spike in short-lived connections (+1200/min), slot_hold_count rose from baseline 4 -> 24, prefetch_queue_growth to 600, effective batch size dropped 3x, p99 latency increased from 180ms -> 1.4s for the route.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:27 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer submitted case with screenshots of Console p99 spike and sample logs. Marked P1 due to dedicated pool impact.

2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Initial triage — confirmed sidecar connection churn correlated with slot_hold_count rise. Hypothesis: sidecar connection resets left slots in a transient HELD_BY_SIDECAR state until lease expiry, preventing prefetch attach and reducing batching efficiency.
2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - Customer (DataMuse): Confirmed they had recently deployed a client change that multiplexes many tiny requests rather than batching. Willing to roll back if necessary.

2026-03-10 13:22 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Applied mitigation #1: reduced sidecar connection timeout and increased socket backlog to reduce reset storms. Observed partial recovery in throughput (tokens/sec +25%).

2026-03-10 13:48 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Applied mitigation #2: temporarily lowered autoscaler grow threshold for this reserved pool (allow faster reacts to queue spikes). Throughput returned to baseline by 12:55-13:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Engineering (Priya): Patch merged to sidecar to coalesce rapid connects into a short windowed-attach operation (PR #412). Backport scheduled to v1.5.x.
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Customer (DataMuse): Confirmed good recovery and accepted compensating configuration changes; requested post-incident notes and preventive recommendations.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Sidecar rapid connect/disconnects were leaving ephemeral markers that scheduler treated as active holds; lease expiry (30s) is long relative to connection churn leading to effective slot underutilization.

Hypothesis B: Prefetch tasks are serialized to a single attach step which collides when many short streams compete; backlog prevents new batches from forming and autoscaler thresholds are tuned for sustained load, not sub-minute microbursts.
Telemetry review: correlation between conn-churn and slot_hold_count is strong (Pearson r=0.78 over 5m window). No GPU OOMs or driver errors detected. NVLink and PCIe metrics normal.
Repro notes: We were able to reproduce a smaller version of the problem in staging by generating 800 short-lived connects/minute and observed a drop in effective batch size and prefetch queue growth.
resolution: Mitigations applied in prod: (1) Reduced sidecar session timeout from 30s -> 8s and increased listen backlog to absorb bursts; (2) Temporarily lowered autoscaler grow threshold and reduced cooldown to allow faster slot allocation; (3) Rolling restart of sidecar-reporter instances to clear reset spike and remove stale holds. A code patch to coalesce attach operations in the sidecar was merged (PR #412) and backported to 1.5.x. The customer reverted the client change that caused extreme multiplexing while we deployed fixes.
follow_up_actions: Deploy sidecar v1.5.4 (contains attach-coalescing) to all reserved pools by 2026-03-18.
Add metric and alert: slot_hold_ratio > 0.15 for 2m -> Pager and create dashboard per reserved pool.
Update autoscaler tuning doc to include microburst window sensitivity and recommended temporary knobs for reserved pools with many small streams.
Add a runbook step: when slot_hold_count rises with conn-churn, perform targeted sidecar restart and consider lowering lease timeout; include safe thresholds and rollback.
Customer guidance: Recommend client-side batching or a short client-side queue to reduce connect churn; include sample SDK config snippet in CS reply.
resolution_notes: Incident closed after validations on 2026-03-12. Root cause is a combination of client-side short-stream fanout plus sidecar behavior that left transient slot holds; autoscaler sensitivity compounded duration. Fixes included configuration mitigations and a sidecar attach coalescing patch.
